paras: My name is Jasmine Marsters. I am half Cook Island, half Tongan, born and raised in South Auckland, and blessed with six beautiful kids.
I compete in strongman, and now, thanks to my eldest daughter, I have recently started learning to play rugby alongside her.

Needing to be strong, not only physically but also mentally, is what attracted me to it. I love it because all I wanted growing up with my brothers was to be as strong as them, and this was a way for me to prove it.

The pros for me are that you get to meet a lot of amazing people, all supporting one another as they put in the work to get the job done. The con for me is that it takes a toll on the body, so listen to it and look after it.
My biggest achievement to date has to be my overhead strength gains. Going from not being able to get a 20 kg bar over my head to now being able to overhead press 75 kg is a big achievement for me.
My ultimate goal is to hit the numbers I set for myself when I started my strongman journey, and one day, if I am able to, compete in an overseas competition.

It was by chance that I got to see Jess at this year's Strongman Series Easter Show, on day 2 of the competition. She was kind enough to let me try the X-ZONE Sports Rub, which honestly helped me out. The instant relief I felt was unbelievable. Ever since then I've been hooked, and it's now a part of my training and recovery routine.

ig.caption:
Strength is built one kilo at a time.

When Jasmine Marsters started strongman, she couldn't get a 20 kg bar over her head. Today she presses 75 kg.

Jasmine is half Cook Island, half Tongan, born and raised in South Auckland, and mum to six. Growing up, all she wanted was to be as strong as her brothers. Now she's proving it on the strongman field, and learning rugby alongside her eldest daughter.

Her advice: strongman takes a toll on the body, so listen to it and look after it.

Jess met Jasmine on day 2 of this year's Strongman Series Easter Show and handed her a pot of Sports Rub to try. In Jasmine's words, "it's now a part of my training and recovery routine."

Read Jasmine's full story, link in bio.
